messages.text: BHA chief predicts 'devastating' impact on racing from Budget tax rise

metadata.summary: British Horseracing Authority chief executive Brant Dunshea has warned the five per cent rise in machine gaming duty for betting shops announced in the Budget will have a “devastating impact” on the future of the sport.
metadata.content: BHA chief Brant Dunshea predicts 'devastating' impact on racing from Budget tax rise | Racing News | Sky Sports Skip to main content BHA chief Brant Dunshea predicts 'devastating' impact on racing from Budget tax rise Following a five per cent increase on Gaming Machine Duty in the latest Budget changes, British Horseracing Authority chief executive Brant Dunshea warned of the potential impacts that the change could have on the industry Wednesday 28 October 2026 16:29, UK Image: BHA chief executive Brant Dunshea British Horseracing Authority chief executive Brant Dunshea has warned the five per cent rise in machine gaming duty for betting shops announced in the Budget will have a “devastating impact” on the future of the sport. Dunshea claimed racing should brace itself for a £57m hit to its finances with reductions in prize money, the loss of thousands of jobs and questions over the viability of racecourses moving forward. "While the government has rejected a worst-case scenario to increase Machine Games Duty to 40 per cent, in raising the rate to 25 per cent it will nevertheless cause significant damage to racing's finances," Branshea said in a statement. "There is now a clear risk that this decision will lead to the closure of hundreds, if not thousands, of betting shops across the country. messages.text: England makes six changes for USA but Kildunne stays on bench

metadata.summary: England have made six changes as they look to halt their two-match losing run when they face the USA in their final WXV Global Series outing in New Jersey.
metadata.content: WXV Global Series: England make six changes for United States match but Ellie Kildunne remains on bench | Rugby Union News | Sky Sports Skip to main content WXV Global Series: England make six changes for United States match but Ellie Kildunne remains on bench England have made six changes for their final WXV Global Series match against the USA on Friday (kick-off 9.15pm GMT); Ellie Kildunne remains on the bench; Red Roses go into match after back-to-back losses to Canada Wednesday 28 October 2026 19:34, UK Image: Ellie Kildunne remains on the bench for the Red Roses England have made six changes as they look to halt their two-match losing run when they face the USA in their final WXV Global Series outing in New Jersey. The Red Roses were beaten in back-to-back games for the first time in a decade when their 41-Test unbeaten run came to an end against Canada, who were then triumphant again a week later. Head coach John Mitchell has reacted to the result in Ottawa by making extensive changes for Friday's match, including a first start for scrum-half Flo Robinson.
